risks.title: Payments just below a quotation threshold may not reflect the full requirement value
risks.statement: Payments that sit just below a quotation threshold warrant checking that the procurement route matched the full value of the requirement.

likelihood.justification: At the three-quote threshold of £{{$.tests.threshold_clustering.tiers[1].threshold}} [rule:CPR-69], {{$.tests.threshold_clustering.tiers[1].count}} payments fall in the band just below it [metric:$.tests.threshold_clustering.tiers[1].count] against {{$.tests.threshold_clustering.tiers[1].comparator.count}} at or just above it [metric:$.tests.threshold_clustering.tiers[1].comparator.count], so there is no excess below the line, and only {{$.tests.threshold_clustering.tiers[1].by_tag.general_procurement.rows}} of the band payments are general procurement [metric:$.tests.threshold_clustering.tiers[1].by_tag.general_procurement.rows]. In the one-quote band [rule:CPR-68] more payments sit below the line than above it, but {{$.tests.threshold_clustering.tiers[0].by_tag.care_or_education_placement.rows}} of the {{$.tests.threshold_clustering.tiers[0].count}} are placement-tagged [metric:$.tests.threshold_clustering.tiers[0].by_tag.care_or_education_placement.rows], and individually chosen placements are exempt from competition [rule:CPR-81]. An isolated indicator: rubric two, the council's Unlikely descriptor [history:LIKELIHOOD-2].

impact.justification: Pricing a requirement just under this threshold would avoid three portal quotations [rule:CPR-69] and a contract notice [rule:CPR-70]. At these values the reasonable worst case fits the council's Minor descriptor: low possibility of legal challenge and a financial consequence in the Minor band [history:IMPACT-2]. Payment values are spend, not loss; no consequence data is available.

risks.proposed_focus: If brought into scope, review quotation evidence for the general-procurement payments just below the three-quote threshold, alongside aggregation testing of the same suppliers.
risks.scope_reason: Payments just below the three-quote threshold do not exceed those at or just above it, and the excess in the one-quote band is mainly placement-tagged; general-procurement rows in the band can be picked up through aggregation testing.

risks.title: Related requirements may not have been aggregated before the procurement route was chosen
risks.statement: Recurring payments to the same supplier within a short window, each below a threshold but together above it, warrant checking whether one requirement was divided across orders.

likelihood.justification: The no-splitting rule is the control [rule:CPR-12]. At the three-quote threshold, {{$.tests.split_purchases.tiers[1].headline.windows}} general-procurement windows of {{$.tests.split_purchases.parameters.window_days}} days combine payments that are each below the threshold [metric:$.tests.split_purchases.tiers[1].headline.windows], across {{$.tests.split_purchases.tiers[1].by_tag.general_procurement.suppliers}} suppliers [metric:$.tests.split_purchases.tiers[1].by_tag.general_procurement.suppliers]; {{$.tests.split_purchases.tiers[2].headline.windows}} general-procurement windows also cross the Key Decision value [metric:$.tests.split_purchases.tiers[2].headline.windows] [rule:CPR-04]. A recurring indicator across suppliers: rubric three, the council's Likely descriptor [history:LIKELIHOOD-3]. Invoicing under contracts already let will explain many windows, and the {{$.tests.split_purchases.tiers[1].placements.windows}} placement windows are reported separately because periodic fees recur [metric:$.tests.split_purchases.tiers[1].placements.windows]. The published data omits smaller payments, so the counts are lower bounds.

impact.justification: Dividing a requirement could bypass three portal quotations [rule:CPR-69] or, at higher values, the report, board and Key Decision route [rule:CPR-66]. The reasonable worst case fits the council's Medium descriptor: reasonable possibility of successful legal challenge or regulatory interest, and external auditor criticism [history:IMPACT-3]. Window totals are spend, not loss; no consequence data is available.

risks.proposed_focus: For sampled general-procurement windows, establish whether the payments formed one requirement; if so, check the route followed against the aggregate value (quotations, portal records, notice and approvals). Set aside windows that are instalments under a contract already let once that contract is confirmed.

risks.title: High-value recurring spend may lack a published or recorded contract award
risks.statement: Suppliers whose annualised spend reaches the contract-notice threshold but who match no published award notice warrant checking against the council's own contract records.

likelihood.justification: Among suppliers whose annualised estimate reaches the notice threshold of £{{$.tests.off_contract.parameters.publication_threshold}} [rule:CPR-70], {{$.tests.off_contract.headline.count}} general-procurement suppliers have no exact match to a published award [metric:$.tests.off_contract.headline.count], against {{$.tests.off_contract.by_match_class.exact.count}} exact matches across all tags [metric:$.tests.off_contract.by_match_class.exact.count]. The indicator recurs across many suppliers: rubric three, the council's Likely descriptor [history:LIKELIHOOD-3]. It is not raised to four because the notice export is not a contract register, the analysis held no rows from the council's own register [metric:$.contracts.register_rows], some publication years are thin, and older, Find a Tender-only or framework awards will not appear. Recording each award on the Contract Register is a control the data cannot see [rule:CPR-35].

impact.justification: {{$.tests.high_value_suppliers.tiers[2].headline.count}} general-procurement suppliers have annualised estimates above £{{$.tests.high_value_suppliers.tiers[2].threshold}} [metric:$.tests.high_value_suppliers.tiers[2].headline.count], and the unmatched top-twenty list includes suppliers in that range, where awards are Key Decisions [rule:CPR-04]. If such spend had no compliant award, the reasonable worst case fits the council's Major descriptor: high possibility of legal challenge and of regulatory intervention [history:IMPACT-4]. Annualised figures are estimates, and spend is not loss.

risks.proposed_focus: Request the council's contract register. For sampled unmatched general-procurement suppliers above the notice threshold, obtain the contract, its term and value, and the notice or recorded exemption; confirm near matches before treating them as unmatched. Suppliers below the notice threshold are outside this test and are not to be questioned on it.

risks.title: Duplicate supplier payments may not be prevented or detected
risks.statement: Payments to the same supplier for exactly the same amount within a short window warrant matching to invoices before any conclusion is drawn.

likelihood.justification: Among general-procurement payments, {{$.tests.duplicates.tiers.different_time.by_tag.general_procurement.rows}} groups of same-supplier, same-amount payments made at different times within {{$.tests.duplicates.parameters.window_days}} days [metric:$.tests.duplicates.tiers.different_time.by_tag.general_procurement.rows] span {{$.tests.duplicates.tiers.different_time.by_tag.general_procurement.suppliers}} suppliers [metric:$.tests.duplicates.tiers.different_time.by_tag.general_procurement.suppliers], with {{$.tests.duplicates.tiers.same_timestamp.by_tag.general_procurement.rows}} further groups inside single payment runs [metric:$.tests.duplicates.tiers.same_timestamp.by_tag.general_procurement.rows]. A recurring indicator across suppliers: rubric three, the council's Likely descriptor [history:LIKELIHOOD-3]. Most flagged groups overall are placement-tagged, where identical periodic fees are expected, and are not counted here. Accounts Payable received Reasonable Assurance [history:AUD-15], which is not adverse and gives no uplift; no contract rule addresses duplicate payment directly.

impact.justification: Value beyond the first payment in the different-time general-procurement groups is £{{$.tests.duplicates.tiers.different_time.by_tag.general_procurement.gbp}} [metric:$.tests.duplicates.tiers.different_time.by_tag.general_procurement.gbp], an indicator rather than confirmed loss. Genuine duplicates are normally recoverable from suppliers, so the reasonable worst case net loss fits the council's Minor descriptor [history:IMPACT-2].

risks.proposed_focus: For sampled general-procurement groups, match each payment to a distinct invoice and order; where a genuine duplicate is found, confirm it was detected and recovered. Review placement-tagged groups only by exception.

risks.title: Spend may continue after a published contract term without an approved extension
risks.statement: Suppliers paid in the period whose every matched notice had ended before the period began warrant checking for an approved extension or a newer contract.

likelihood.justification: {{$.tests.expired_notice_spend.count}} suppliers were paid in the period although every matching published notice had ended before it began [metric:$.tests.expired_notice_spend.count]; extending a contract needs S151 approval [rule:CPR-78]. A small set, mostly of low spend: an isolated indicator, rubric two, the council's Unlikely descriptor [history:LIKELIHOOD-2]. A newer contract may exist without a notice in the export.

impact.justification: Spend with these suppliers in the period is £{{$.tests.expired_notice_spend.gbp}} [metric:$.tests.expired_notice_spend.gbp]. An unapproved extension at this scale fits the council's Minor descriptor: low possibility of legal challenge [history:IMPACT-2]. Spend is not loss.

risks.proposed_focus: For each flagged supplier, obtain the current contract or the extension and its S151 approval; record where a newer award explains the payments.

risks.title: Spend may exceed the awarded contract value without an approved variation
risks.statement: Suppliers whose annualised spend runs well above the annual rate of their single published award warrant checking for an approved variation.

likelihood.justification: {{$.tests.spend_vs_award.count}} suppliers have annualised spend at least {{$.tests.spend_vs_award.parameters.ratio_min}} times the annual rate of their single published award [metric:$.tests.spend_vs_award.count]; variations need prior Monitoring Officer and S151 approval [rule:CPR-79], or board approval above the Threshold [rule:CPR-80]. Several flags rest on one or two payments, where annualising one quarter can overstate the run-rate, and award values may be estimates or maxima. An isolated indicator: rubric two, the council's Unlikely descriptor [history:LIKELIHOOD-2]. Most suppliers could not be tested because they lack a unique active notice [metric:$.tests.spend_vs_award.excluded.no_unique_active_notice].

impact.justification: Spend with flagged suppliers in the period is £{{$.tests.spend_vs_award.gbp}} [metric:$.tests.spend_vs_award.gbp]. Spend beyond an award without an approved variation fits the council's Medium descriptor: reasonable possibility of successful legal challenge and external audit criticism [history:IMPACT-3]. This is spend, not loss.

risks.proposed_focus: For each flagged supplier, compare spend with the award value, term and scope, and obtain any approved variation; confirm whether the published award value is an estimate or a maximum.

risks.title: Waivers and exceptions may not be authorised and documented as the rules require
risks.statement: Waivers of competition and exceptions to the rules cannot be seen in spend data; whether they were approved in advance, at the right level and fully documented needs direct testing.

likelihood.justification: Only the Monitoring Officer and/or S151 Officer may grant a waiver, and only in advance [rule:CPR-21], yet another clause lets the relevant Executive Director or the Chief Executive waive competition at discretion [rule:CPR-20]; that conflict in the rules can lead to approval at the wrong level. Every waiver must be fully documented [rule:CPR-25] and approved by the S151 Officer [rule:CPR-27]. No metric observes waivers, so this is rated on the rules and the gap. A rule-only control would be rubric one; the design conflict raises it to two, the council's Unlikely descriptor [history:LIKELIHOOD-2].

impact.justification: A waiver removes competition altogether; for higher-value contracts the reasonable worst case fits the council's Medium descriptor: reasonable possibility of successful legal challenge and external audit criticism [history:IMPACT-3] [rule:CPR-21]. No waiver data is available to size the exposure.

risks.proposed_focus: Obtain the waiver and exception register. For a sample, confirm advance approval by the officer the rules require, the documented reasons, the S151 record and, where needed, the board exception report. Check whether unmatched high-value suppliers appear on the register.

risks.title: Higher-value awards may not carry the decision and approval the rules require
risks.statement: Contracts above the Key Decision value need Key Decision, board and Executive approvals that spend data cannot show; these need direct testing on contract files.

likelihood.justification: Awards over £{{$.tests.high_value_suppliers.tiers[2].threshold}} must be taken as Key Decisions [rule:CPR-04], with board-approved reports in the middle band [rule:CPR-66] and Executive approval at the top band [rule:CPR-67]. No metric observes approvals and no adverse audit history exists; contract letting received Reasonable Assurance [history:AUD-01]. A rule-only control with no adverse evidence: rubric one, the council's Rare descriptor [history:LIKELIHOOD-1].

impact.justification: {{$.tests.high_value_suppliers.tiers[2].headline.count}} general-procurement suppliers have annualised estimates above that value [metric:$.tests.high_value_suppliers.tiers[2].headline.count]. An award at that scale without the required decision fits the council's Major descriptor: high possibility of legal challenge and of regulatory intervention [history:IMPACT-4].

risks.proposed_focus: For high-value suppliers sampled under the notice-coverage test, check the decision record, board report and Forward Plan or Executive approval against the value band.

risks.title: Placement purchasing outside competition may lack the recorded justification the rules require
risks.statement: Individually chosen care and education placements are exempt from competition, but the rules still require recorded reasons for the provider choice, which spend data cannot show.

likelihood.justification: The reasons for the choice of provider must be kept on the case notes [rule:CPR-81]; spend data cannot see case notes, so this is rated on the rule and the gap. Placement-tagged spend is the largest tag in the data [metric:$.population.tags.care_or_education_placement.gbp] and dominates the split and duplicate indicators, which periodic fees largely explain. Personal Budgets (Direct Payments) received Limited Assurance [history:AUD-16]: adjacent adverse evidence, not a repeat finding on this theme, so no uplift applies, but it lifts the rule-only rubric one to two, the council's Unlikely descriptor [history:LIKELIHOOD-2]. Purchase of residential and nursing care received Reasonable Assurance [history:AUD-18].

impact.justification: A poorly justified provider choice affects vulnerable people and value for money; the reasonable worst case fits the council's Medium descriptor: external agency criticism, for example by an inspectorate, and reasonable possibility of regulatory interest [history:IMPACT-3]. No consequence data is available.

risks.proposed_focus: If brought into scope, sample placement-tagged payments, prioritising children's and education placements outside the recent care-purchasing audit, and check the recorded reasons for the provider choice.
risks.scope_reason: Adult residential and nursing care purchasing was audited recently with Reasonable Assurance, and the Limited opinion on direct payments is best pursued through audit follow-up; the auditor may bring children's and education placements into scope.

excluded.reason: Above-threshold advertising, tender and award routes (CPR-10, CPR-13, CPR-74) cannot be tested: the statutory threshold parameters are null in rules.json and analytics computed no statutory tier. The auditor should supply the figures and their source.
E-tendering, late tenders and evaluation (CPR-13 to CPR-18) are rule-only with no metric; contract letting received Reasonable Assurance (AUD-01). Testable on files if the auditor extends scope.

excluded.id: Contract documents, sealing, bonds and insurance
excluded.reason: Minimum clauses, sealing, bonds and insurance (CPR-33 to CPR-62) are rule-only content controls with no metric or history; they can be checked on contract files pulled for in-scope risks.

Spend publication (CPR-05) is evidenced by the published data itself; ITT publication, board reporting and social value (CPR-01, CPR-06, CPR-08) have no metric or history. Register completeness (CPR-07, CPR-35) is handled under notice coverage.

Advice before use and approval without further competition (CPR-28, CPR-77) are rule-only; framework call-offs cannot be identified reliably in spend data and are treated as a known reason for missing notices.
Clause 1.6.2 treats grants as contracts but rules.json excludes it as a definition, so no testable rule applies; grant spend is reported separately in analytics.
RT-01, RT-08, RT-09 and RT-12 name fraud generally, not procurement; the Anti-Fraud Work Plan is not in the papers. Fraud-relevant patterns are covered by the indicator risks.

No repeat finding exists on any rated theme: no agreed actions are published and no theme has a prior adverse opinion followed by another. AUD-16 (Limited) is used as adjacent evidence, not an uplift.
